sentences.text:
This is second bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.306/2023 dated 19.5.2023, registered at Police Station - Banda,
District- Sagar (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 498A, 304B/34 of IPC and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
He is in detention since 24.05.2023.

His first bail application was dismissed as withdrawn and not pressed vide order dated 19.03.2024 passed in M.Cr.C.No.10016 of 2024.
2.

As per the prosecution story, on 12.04.2023, Smt. Arti w/o Nanhelal @ Chotu Singh Ahirwar,
aged 23 years, committed suicide by hanging herself.
In the course of investigation it was found that on 25.5.2018 deceased by eloping with Nanhelal @ Chotu Singh had solemnized married.
She was satisfied with the marriage and for a period of five years, they remained together without any complaint in matrimonial home.

It was alleged that after five years of marriage, husband and Nanhelal @ Chhotu Ahirwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23655257/
1 mother-in-law started to demand Rs.2 Lacs for establishing the business of Nanhelal and shifted to Sagar by leaving her in the house of elder brother of husband.

sentences.text: After investigation, charge sheet has been filed.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
He is the husband of the deceased.
Marriage was a love marriage and therefore, no question of demand of dowry arises.
Deceased committed suicide as she was having some differences with him.
Parents of the deceased have already been examined before the trial Court.
They have turned hostile and not supported prosecution story.
Co-accused has already been released on bail by this Court vide order dated 31.08.2023 passed in M.Cr.C.No.38716 of 2023.Therefore, it is prayed that applicant too may be released on bail.
4 . O n the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the grant of bail.

5 . Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, including the change in circumstances, but without expressing any opinion on the merit of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which applicant may be released on bail.
Consequently, this second bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

6 . I t is directed that applicant - Nanhelal @ Chhotu Ahirwar be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
7 .
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case o f bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE b Nanhelal @ Chhotu Ahirwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23655257/
